questions.question: In the Harappan site of Chanhudaro, the main specialized activity was:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bead manufacturing**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Chanhudaro is an important Harappan site located in present-day Sindh, Pakistan, and is known for its specialization in bead manufacturing during the Indus Valley Civilization.
 
• The site is famous for its advanced techniques in making beads from semi-precious stones such as carnelian, agate, jasper, and steatite.
 
• Bead production at Chanhudaro involved intricate processes such as cutting, drilling, polishing, and coloring, showcasing the high level of craftsmanship achieved by the Harappans.
 
• Archaeological findings suggest the presence of bead workshops, tools, and raw materials, indicating that bead manufacturing was a key economic activity in the region.
 
• Beads produced at Chanhudaro were widely traded across the Indus Valley region and beyond, highlighting the site's significance in the Harappan trade network.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Textile Production:**

 
 
• While textile production was an important activity in the Indus Valley Civilization, it was not the specialized activity at Chanhudaro.
 
• The Harappans were skilled in producing cotton textiles, evidenced by the discovery of cotton fragments at Harappan sites like Mohenjo-Daro.
 
• They used spinning wheels and dyes obtained from plants to produce colorful textiles, which were likely traded extensively.
 
 
 
• **Agriculture:**
 
 
• Agriculture was a fundamental aspect of the Indus Valley Civilization, with crops such as wheat, barley, and pulses being cultivated.
 
• The Harappans practiced advanced irrigation techniques and plowing methods to sustain their agricultural economy.
 
• While agriculture was prevalent across the civilization, it was not a specialized activity at Chanhudaro.
 
 
 
• **Making Stone Tools:**
 
 
• Stone tools were commonly used by the Harappans for various purposes, including hunting, farming, and construction.
 
• Sites like Burzahom in Kashmir are more closely associated with the production of stone tools rather than Chanhudaro.
 
• Chanhudaro's specialization in bead manufacturing makes it distinct from other Harappan sites focused on stone tool production.
 
 
 
• **Main Theme - The Indus Valley Civilization:**
 
 
• The Indus Valley Civilization (2600–1900 BCE) was one of the world's earliest urban civilizations, known for its planned cities, advanced drainage systems, and trade networks.
 
• Key sites include Mohenjo-Daro, Harappa, Lothal, Dholavira, and Chanhudaro, each known for specific activities and contributions to the civilization.
 
• Specialized activities, such as bead manufacturing at Chanhudaro, highlight the diversity and sophistication of industries in the Harappan era.

questions.question: 'Daimabad', a Harappan site, is located in which state?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Maharashtra**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Daimabad** is an important archaeological site belonging to the **Harappan Civilization**, located in the state of **Maharashtra**.
 
• It is situated in the **Ahmednagar district**, near the Pravara River, which is a tributary of the Godavari River.
 
• The site was discovered in **1958** by B.P. Bopardikar, and further excavations were carried out by the Archaeological Survey of India (ASI).
 
• It is known for its unique findings of **bronze artifacts** like the bronze chariot, which are considered rare in Harappan sites.
 
• Daimabad is significant as it marks the **southernmost extent** of the Harappan Civilization, showcasing its geographical reach.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Harappan Civilization:**

 
 
• The Harappan Civilization, also known as the **Indus Valley Civilization**, flourished between **2600 BCE to 1900 BCE**.
 
• It was spread across modern-day **Pakistan** and parts of **India**, including states like Gujarat, Rajasthan, Punjab, Haryana, and Maharashtra.
 
• The civilization is renowned for its **urban planning**, advanced drainage systems, and unique artifacts.
 
• Major Harappan sites include **Harappa**, **Mohenjo-Daro**, **Dholavira**, **Rakhigarhi**, and **Lothal**.
 
 
 
• **Daimabad Excavations:**
 
 
• The excavations revealed a **large settlement** with structures resembling Harappan architecture, including brick platforms and drainage systems.
 
• Significant findings include **terracotta figurines**, pottery, seals, and tools.
 
• The discovery of **bronze objects**, such as a chariot, a figure of an elephant, and a buffalo, suggests advanced metallurgical techniques.
 
• These artifacts indicate possible cultural exchanges between the Harappan Civilization and other contemporary societies.
 
 
 
• **Geographical Spread of Harappan Sites:**
 
 
• While Harappa and Mohenjo-Daro are located in **Pakistan**, sites like **Rakhigarhi** and **Lothal** are situated in modern-day India.
 
• Daimabad, being the **southernmost Harappan site**, highlights the extent of the civilization into the Deccan Plateau.
 
 
 
• **Other Harappan Sites in India:**
 
 
• **Lothal:** Located in Gujarat, famous for its dockyard and trade links.
 
• **Dholavira:** Also in Gujarat, known for its water conservation systems.
 
• **Rakhigarhi:** Located in Haryana, one of the largest known Harappan sites.

questions.question: Which of the following was not a Indus valley civilization site?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Magadh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **__Important Points__**

__
 
• Magadha was an ancient Indian kingdom in southern Bihar.
 
• It was counted as one of the sixteen Mahajanapadas of ancient India. 
 
• The Maurya Empire and Gupta Empire of Ancient history originated in Magadha.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__** 

__
 
• **Lothal: **

 
 
• Excavated by **S.R Rao** in **1953**.
 
• It was situated in Gujarat on the **Bhogva river** near the Gulf of Cambay.
 
• Important findings are the first manmade port, dockyard, rice husk, fire altars, chess playing.
 
 
 
• Mohenjo-Daro (the literal meaning of the term is - mount of the dead)
 
 
• ​Excavated by R.D Banerji in **1922**.
 
• Situated on the Bank of river Indus in Larkana district of Punjab (Pakistan).
 
• Important findings are the great bath granary, bronze dancing girl, a seal of Pasupathi Mahadeva, a steatite statue of beard man, a piece of woven cotton.
 
 
 
• Dholavira:
 
 
• Located on the bank of **Luni river** in Rann of Kutch.
 
• Discovered by **JP Joshi (1967-68)**.
 
• Important finding - Exclusive water management.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Indus Valley Civilization was spread from present-day North-East Afghanistan to Pakistan and North-West India.
 
• The civilization flourished in the river basins of the Ghaggar-Hakra river and the Indus.
 
• Indus valley civilization is one of the four oldest civilizations in the world.
 
• It is also known as Harappan Civilization and is well-known for its organized planning based on the grid system.
 
• There are seven important cities in the Indus valley civilization:
 
 
• Mohanjodaro
 
• Harappa
 
• Kalibangan
 
• Lothal
 
• Chanhudaru
 
• Dholavira
 
• Banawali

questions.question: The first astronomical observatory related to Harappan civilization was found at which place?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Dholavira**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The first astronomical observatory related to the Harappan civilization was found at **Dholavira in the Kutch district of Gujarat.**
 
• It was discovered in **1967-68 by J.P Joshi.**
 
• Scientist's identified two circular structures used for observational astronomy during the Harappan Civilisation. 
 
• **Dholavira** is the larger of the two most remarkable excavations of the Indus Valley Civilization or Harappan culture.
 
• It is **one of the five largest Harappan sites** and **most prominent archaeological sites in India.**
 
• Excavations from Dholavira includes
 
 
• gold, silver, terracotta ornaments
 
• pottery
 
• bronze vessels
 
• a large number of antiquities such as animal bones, etc
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Dholavira has been nominated by the Government to be included in World Heritage List for the year 2020.

questions.question: Indus Valley Civilization was a ________ age civilization.
questions.solution: Indus valley civilisation was a Bronze Age civilisation. The Bronze Age in the Indian subcontinent begins around 3000 BCE and in the end gives rise to the Indus Valley Civilization, which had its (mature) period between 2600 BCE to 1900 BCE.

questions.question: Banawali, an Indus Valley civilization site, is in which district of Haryana?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Fatehabad district**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] Important Points__** 

 
• The Indus Valley Civilization was a civilization that was mostly founded in the Indus River Valley.
 
• The time period of the Indus Valley Civilization was from 2600 BC to 1900 BC.
 
• The term Indus valley civilization was coined by John Marshall.
 
• This civilization was spread over Sindh, Baluchistan, Haryana, Rajasthan, Punjab, Western Uttar Pradesh, and Northern Maharashtra.
 
• The important sites of the Indus Valley Civilization were Harappa, Mohenjodaro, Chanhudaro, Lothal, Kalibanga, Banawali, Dholavira, Rangpur, etc.
 
• Banawali
 
 
• Banawali site was excavated by R.S.Bist in 1973 in Fatehabad, Haryana.
 
• The Replica of the plough was field found in the Banawali district.
 
• The clay figure of the mother goddess was also found there.
 
 
 
• Kalibangan
 
 
• Kalibangan means the bangles of black colour.
 
• It was first excavated by Amalanand Ghosh in 1951 and later B.V.Lal and B.K. Thapar in 1961.
 
• It was excavated in Hanumangarh, Rajasthan.
 
• The evidence of a ploughed field was found here the first time.
 
 
 
• Mohenjodaro
 
 
• ​Mohenjodaro site was excavated by R.D.Banerjee in 1922.
 
• It was situated on the Indus river.
 
• It was excavated in Sindh, Pakistan.
 
• A great bath and a great granary were excavated there.
 
 
 
• Rangpur
 
 
• ​Rangpur is an archaeological site in Gujarat, western India.
 
• It belongs to the period of the Indus valley civilization.
 
• The excavation was started by the Archeological Survey of India during 1931 led by M.S.Vats.
 
 
 
• Lothal Site
 
 
• Lothal was excavated by S.R.Rao in 1954 in Gujarat.
 
• It was a port city as evidence shows.
 
• The evidence of ​the dockyard was found at Lothal.
 
 
 
• Dholavira Site
 
 
• It was excavated by J.P.Joshi in 1967 near the Kutchh area of Gujarat.
 
• A unique water harnessing system was founded at the Dholavira site.
 
• Dholavira has yielded the longest inscription comprising ten large-sized signs of the Harappan script.
 
• It was embedded on a three-meter-long board
